story.title: In Musandam, a Children's Story Series Brings Whales, Dolphins, and Marine Conservation into the Classroom

detail.extracted_title: In Musandam, a Children's Story Series Brings Whales, Dolphins, and Marine Conservation into the Classroom
detail.excerpt: Launched at the Musandam Culture and Innovation Center in Khasab under the "Bi'ati" initiative, "Khalid's Journey in the Sea of Tales" uses storytelling to connect young students with the governorate's marine wildlife.
detail.article_html:
In Musandam, the sea is part of every child's daily horizon—from the deep limestone inlets of Khasab to the fishing coves of Bukha and Qada. Now, environmental specialists and educators in the governorate are turning that familiar coastline into a series of illustrated children's stories designed to teach young readers how to protect the marine life beneath the surface.

At the Grand Hall of the Musandam Culture and Innovation Center in Wilayat Khasab, the Environment Department in Musandam Governorate launched the environmental storytelling series "Khalid's Journey in the Sea of Tales" (Rihlat Khalid fi Bahr Al Hikayat) as part of its "Bi'ati" (My Environment) initiative. Held under the patronage of Salim bin Humaid Al Junaibi, Director of the Environment Department in Musandam, the launch brought together teachers, environmental engineers, and school students from across the governorate.

Turning Young Readers into Partners in Marine Protection

Ruqayya bint Hassan Al Shehhi, Media Specialist and Project Manager of the "Bi'ati" initiative, explained that the series was built on a simple observation: children absorb environmental ethics far more deeply through characters, adventures, and narrative situations than through direct instruction alone.

Through the eyes of its young protagonist, "Khalid's Journey in the Sea of Tales" introduces children to the marine creatures that inhabit Musandam's waters—particularly the dolphins and whales that play an essential role in maintaining the local marine ecosystem. At the same time, the stories prompt children to examine everyday human habits, showing the damage caused by throwing plastic waste into the water or leaving abandoned fishing nets drifting across reefs.

Connecting Fiction to the Musandam Nature Reserve

To bridge the stories on the page with the real-world geography outside the hall, Eng. Noura bint Abdullah Al Shehhi, Head of the Vegetation Cover and Biodiversity Section at the Musandam Environment Department, led an interactive presentation on the ecological value of the Musandam Nature Reserve Park.

She walked students through the unique marine species and natural habitats protected within the reserve, emphasizing that safeguarding Musandam's coastal biodiversity is a shared responsibility connecting government institutions, schools, and families.

A Foundation for Environmental Education in Local Schools

From the classroom perspective, Makkiyah bint Hassan Al Kumzari, Assistant Principal of Qada Basic Education School, welcomed the series as an early foundation for Omani environmental education—one that she hopes will be distributed across schools nationwide.

When a student imagines himself as a character who rescues marine life and keeps local beaches clean, Al Kumzari noted, conservation stops being an abstract classroom rule and becomes a daily habit practiced along Musandam's shores.

detail.instagram_caption:
At the Musandam Culture and Innovation Center in Wilayat Khasab, the Environment Department in Musandam Governorate launched a new children's storytelling series titled "Khalid's Journey in the Sea of Tales" under the "Bi'ati" (My Environment) initiative. Held under the patronage of Salim bin Humaid Al Junaibi, the program brings together environmental specialists and local educators to connect young readers with the marine wildlife of northern Oman.

Led by project manager Ruqayya bint Hassan Al Shehhi and biodiversity section head Eng. Noura bint Abdullah Al Shehhi, the series introduces school students to the whales, dolphins, and coral habitats of the Musandam Nature Reserve while illustrating the dangers of marine litter and abandoned fishing nets.

Educators including Makkiyah bint Hassan Al Kumzari of Qada Basic Education School see the storytelling series as a practical model for environmental education across Omani classrooms, encouraging children to imagine themselves as everyday guardians of their coastline.
